Overview

ART.stdf (Automatic Report Tool) is a software designed to process MDRF .stdf files in engineering, aiming to simplify daily work.

Note: This is ALPHA release so some bug are inside.

Welcome to the ART Technical Documentation

  • Progress Condition
  • Progress Stability check
  • Progress Volume parameter
  • Interactive Shmoo
  • Characterization Report

The level of detail in the reports varies according to the type of report requested. This may include a report by flow, a report for each composite, or a report for each individual test.

ART is a powerful analysis tool running on a dedicated PC in Catania, designed to deliver high-performance data processing and insightful reporting.
Developed entirely in Python, ART leverages cutting-edge technologies to provide a robust, flexible, and user-friendly platform for deep insights into complex datasets.

Core Technologies

Polars DataFrame

ART utilizes Polars, a lightning-fast DataFrame library engineered to utilize all available CPU cores, optimize queries to reduce unnecessary work and memory allocations, handle datasets much larger than available RAM, and provide a consistent and predictable API. Written from the ground up with performance in mind, Polars is recognized as one of the fastest data processing solutions on a single machine. The library comes with zero required dependencies and features incredibly fast import times, making it significantly more efficient than traditional Pandas for large-scale data operations.

Plotly

All reports generated by ART leverage Plotly's Python graphing library to create interactive, publication-quality graphs. Plotly enables users to explore data through features like zooming, accessing additional details, and clicking for deeper insights, while handling JavaScript interactivity behind the scenes. Users can effortlessly export graphs as images, highlight specific data points, and explore detailed numeric summaries, significantly enhancing data exploration and decision-making capabilities.

Apache Parquet

Data is stored in Apache Parquet, an open-source, column-oriented data file format designed for efficient data storage and retrieval, providing high-performance compression and encoding schemes to handle complex data in bulk. The columnar storage approach allows Parquet to read only the needed columns, greatly minimizing I/O operations. This targeted approach helps reduce query times from hours to minutes while significantly lowering storage costs, making it naturally suited for tabular data structures and ensuring optimal performance during data retrieval and processing.


This combination of high-performance computing technologies ensures ART delivers exceptional speed, interactivity, and scalability for even the most demanding analytical workloads.

Stability

Input File Requirements

The Stability report analyzes the STDF file of a single part containing 30 test loops. If you need to analyze multiple parts or more loops, please consolidate all relevant data into a single STDF file for processing.

    \\gpm-pe-data.gnb.st.com\ENGI_MCD_STDF
    • <PRODUCT>
      • <PRODUCTCUT>
        • <FLOW>
          • <PKG or LOT>
            • PKG or LOT _ BADGE or WAFER
              • LOOP
                • file.std.gz
              • LOOP_VALx
              • LOOP_VALy


If need to save different VAL you can rename old folder like "_VAL<number>"

It is best to use the .std.gz extension to reduce storage space and processing time.
Please compress your STDF files and rename them using the above extension

Purpose and Metrics

The Stability report focuses on evaluating the consistency and reliability of the manufacturing process over repeated test loops. The key quality criterion for parametric tests is a Process Capability index (Cp) greater than 10, indicating excellent process stability. For functional tests, the requirement is zero failures to ensure functional integrity across loops.

Report Content

For each composite tested, the ART tool generates a dedicated report including:

  • Parametric Tests:
    • A histogram illustrating the distribution of measurement values across loops.
    • A statistics table summarizing key metrics such as Cp and other relevant parameters.
  • Functional Tests:
    • A Pareto chart displaying the count of passes and fails, highlighting dominant failure modes if any.

Conclusions

The report conclusion section provides:

  • Identification of any parametric or functional tests failing to meet the specified criteria (Cp < 10 or any functional failures).
  • Summary tables consolidating the overall stability assessment across all composites and tests.

Example

For a practical example, please refer to the Progress Mosquito 512K report:
44EY HSI Stability Report

Volume IP Report

Purpose and Metrics

The Volume IP report is designed for volume validation, assessing process capability and yield across a larger dataset. The key quality criterion for parametric tests is a Process Capability index (CpK) greater than 1.6, ensuring the process is both capable and centered within specifications. For functional tests, the requirement is good yield, indicating a high percentage of units passing functional testing.

Report Content

For each composite, ART generates a separate report that includes:

  • Parametric Tests:
    • A histogram showing the distribution of test results.
    • A statistics table with detailed metrics including Cp, CpK, and other relevant parameters.
  • Functional Tests:
    • A Pareto chart summarizing the number of passes and fails, facilitating identification of predominant failure causes.

Conclusions

The conclusion section of the report:

  • Highlights any parametric or functional tests that do not meet the required specifications.
  • Includes summary tables that provide an overview of the process capability and yield performance across all composites.

Example

For further reference, see the Progress Mosquito 512K Volume IP report:
44EY HSI Volume IP Report

Test Time Report

Purpose and Metrics

The Test Time report consolidates all test time data extracted from the STDF file into a single comprehensive file. Its goal is to analyze and visualize the distribution and variability of test durations across different composites and individual devices, enabling identification of inefficiencies and potential bottlenecks.

Report Content

The ART tool generates the following visualizations and data summaries:

  • A pie chart illustrating the distribution of total test time among the different composites, providing a clear overview of time allocation.
  • A scatter plot displaying the test time of each individual device, which helps to identify outliers or excessively long test times potentially caused by timeouts or test failures.
  • For each composite:
    • An histogram showing the distribution of test times to detect large variations or deviations during the entire test process.
    • A Pareto chart summarizing the average execution time per sub-test, highlighting which sub-tests contribute most to the overall test duration and where optimization efforts should be focused.

Conclusions

The conclusion section presents all relevant data in tabular form, including:Minimum, average, maximum, and standard deviation of test times for each composite.

Example

For reference, please consult the Progress Mosquito 512K Test Time report:
44EY Test Time Report

Yield Report

Purpose and Metrics

The Yield report evaluates the production yield, monitoring its trend over time to provide insights into manufacturing performance and stability. It analyzes yield data segmented by hardware bin and software bin, enabling detailed identification of yield issues related to both physical and logical classifications.

Report Content

The ART tool generates the following analyses and visualizations:

  • A trend chart showing the yield progression over time, useful for detecting improvements or degradations in production quality.
  • Yield breakdown by hardware bin and software bin, providing a granular view of yield distribution across different classification bins.
  • A wafer map visualizing the spatial distribution of software bin results across the wafer, helping to identify localized yield issues or patterns.

Conclusions

The conclusion section includes:

  • Summary tables displaying yield percentages for each hardware and software bin.
  • Identification of bins or time periods with yield degradation or anomalies.
  • Insights to guide corrective actions and process improvements aimed at yield enhancement.

Example

For reference, please consult the Progress Mosquito 512K Yield report:
44EY Yield Report

Shmoo

Input File Requirements

For the T2000 platform, it is possible to save .shm files and generate an interactive report that allows dynamic visualization of the shmoo data. Each shmoo must have its own dedicated .shm file to ensure proper analysis.
The shmoos are combined into a single file, the report will automatically highlight the nominal test conditions, including the test program version and date, to facilitate quick identification and comparison.

Characterization

Main Function

Characterization reports utilize a multi-STDF approach to generate multiple types of reports that highlight variations across process corners, temperature ranges, and test conditions.
This methodology enables comprehensive analysis by correlating data from different environmental and operational parameters, providing deeper insights into device performance and reliability.
For multi-STDF analysis, a separate file is generated for each test, clearly highlighting the associated process, temperature conditions, and test condition variations. To ensure consistency and facilitate automated processing, there are established guidelines for naming the test files and for organizing the different STDF files within the project structure. Adhering to these conventions is essential to enable accurate correlation of test data and to streamline the review process.



Report

There are two main types of reports generated: parametric reports and functional reports.

  • Parametric Reports: These reports display data values on the X-axis and the Y-axis representing different process corners, while the vertical axis is split according to the various test conditions. Temperature is visually distinguished using a color scheme ranging from cold to hot: blue for cold, green for ambient, and red for hot.
    All parametric tests are graphically represented using box plots, which include pre-processed statistical data such as mean, median, standard deviation, variance, interquartile range (IQR), kurtosis, as well as upper and lower fences. This comprehensive set of statistical parameters facilitates detailed analysis of parameter distributions and helps identify trends, outliers, and potential anomalies under different conditions.

    At the end of the report, a summary table is provided to clearly highlight the corresponding current, temperature, and test condition for each data set, enabling quick cross-reference and comparison.

  • Functional Reports: Functional test results are presented using scatter plots based on yield for each test condition. This allows quick assessment of functional performance variability across different process corner and temerature.



Naming convention

Test Program requirment

For tests requiring modifications in test conditions, it is necessary to update the test program and duplicate the test multiple times, adjusting timing and/or voltage levels according to the specified requirements.
Consequently, each variant must have a distinct test name to allow ART to correctly group and generate splits for the different conditions.
To enable this grouping, the following naming convention must be applied:



STDF

Tree path

Unlike other reports, for this report it is important not to nest folders. Instead, there should be one folder per process corner. Each folder is created with a name indicating the lot, wafer, and type of corner.
Inside each corner folder, there should be one STDF file for each temperature condition.
It is recommended to number these files sequentially from 01 to the maximum number of temperature points, ordered from the lowest to the highest temperature. This numbering scheme facilitates easy identification and sorting of temperature-specific data within each corner.

Example folder and file structure:


    \\gpm-pe-data.gnb.st.com\ENGI_MCD_STDF
    • <PRODUCT>
      • <PRODUCTCUT>
        • ...
        • EWSCHAR
          • <LOT_WAFER_CORNER>
            • 01_product_testprogram.std.gz - lower temperature
            • 02_product_testprogram.std.gz
            • ...
            • NN_product_testprogram.std.gz - highest temperature
          • <xxxxxx_01_TTTT>
          • <xxxxxx_02_FFTT>
          • <xxxxxx_03_SSTT>
          • <yyyyyy_01_FSTT>
          • <yyyyyy_02_SFTT>

ID Corner Name Nmos Pmos Resistance Capacitance
FFTT Fast Fast Fast Fast Typical Typical
FFMM Fast Fast RC MIN Fast Fast Minimum Minimum
F1TT Mid Fast Mid Fast Mid Fast Typical Typical
FSTT Fast Slow Fast Slow Typical Typical
TTTT Standard Wafer Typical Typical Typical Typical
SFTT Slow Fast Slow Fast Typical Typical
S1TT Mid Slow Mid Slow Mid Slow Typical Typical
SSXX Slow Slow RC MAX Slow Slow Maximum Maximum
SSTT Slow Slow Slow Slow Typical Typical
